title: Why Are 96,000,000 Black Balls on This Reservoir?
beats: Shade balls shown; narrator says their main purpose is NOT evaporation, as you may have heard
Promise to visit the biggest pile on earth; put on life vest and climb into the boat
Rapid-fire list of the viewer's questions: why black, safe, cost, evaporation, real purpose
Driving the boat through the balls: they are water-filled so they wobble and resist wind, then pack into crystal-like rafts
Absurdity of a world-size ball pit; tap water at home comes from here
Problem begins: harmless bromide plus ozone becomes carcinogenic bromate; regulation only tests at the filter plant
Beverage customer reports high bromate that the plant never saw; reservoir tests show it jumps on entering open air
Three ingredients (bromide, chlorine, sunlight): only sunlight can be removed; tarps, PVC trampoline, pipe raft, chipped pipe all rejected
Found existing product: bird balls from mine ponds and airports; birds vanished once deployed
Three kiddie pools (sun, tarp, balls) with reservoir water; balls fix bromate immediately
Why black: carbon black lasts 10+ years; blue dyes tested and failed; HDPE is milk-jug plastic, food grade
Boat sits still in a breeze, like peanut butter; side benefits: no algae, almost no chlorine
Return to evaporation: black should heat water, but cover cuts surface area and airflow, bottom stays cool, air gap like double-paned window; 80-90% reduction
Cost about 33 cents each, partly repaid by chlorine and evaporation savings
Hexagonal interlocking balls rejected: need to spread out and not perch on the bank as level changes

metrics.misconception: yes: balls exist to cut evaporation (0:00), and black should heat water (8:57)
metrics.brute_force: yes 4:39: engineers list failed covers (tarps, PVC trampoline, pipe raft, chipped pipe) before finding balls
metrics.examples: 3 cover options rejected, then 1 solution; three tested pools; no scaling
metrics.ending: No recap, no sponsor. Ends on a boba joke about the pool-of-boba look; the evaporation myth was closed at 8:57-10:02.

principles.1: confirmed: opens on a boat ride, kids' ball pit, milk jug, double-paned window, tap water at home (2:44)
principles.2: not-observed: no notation; only one new term, bromate, introduced late (3:16)
principles.4: partly: double-paned window analogy at 9:29 for air-gap insulation, but little rigor follows
principles.5: confirmed: narrator literally drives the boat through the balls to feel the wobble and drag (1:09, 7:51)
principles.6: confirmed: the reservoir team's failed brute-force covers come before the shade ball (4:39)
principles.7: partly: viewer can infer 'must be sunlight' from the three-ingredient list at 4:23 before it is stated, and the kiddie-pool test at 6:32 is a visible controlled comparison
principles.8: not-observed: speech and idea rate stay brisk; no clear slowdown
principles.10: partly: kiddie pools test a tiny version before the full reservoir (6:17)
principles.11: confirmed: problem (bromate) is built first, then constraint (only sunlight is removable), then solution (balls), then secondary questions
principles.12: confirmed: bird balls from mines and airports, milk jugs, beverage company, boba
principles.13: partly: every answer is plain-language by a practitioner, with reasons for rejecting alternatives (blue dye, hexagons, tarps)

new_moves.name: question-backlog-then-pay-off
new_moves.what: Narrator lists five viewer questions up front and then answers each in the field, saving the hardest (evaporation) for last

new_moves.name: engineer-rejection-ladder
new_moves.what: Domain expert walks a ladder of rejected options, each failing for a stated reason, so the final design looks forced rather than clever

new_moves.name: cheap-controlled-test
new_moves.what: Show the humblest experiment that proved the claim: three kiddie pools as control, tarp and treatment

theory: The video teaches by running a detective story through a physical place: odd object, apparent purpose, real purpose, then every question the viewer would raise is answered by a person on site. The insight lands because alternatives are shown failing, so the solution feels necessary. Myths are planted early and defused late to keep tension.
velocity: Scene builder: a 'rejection ladder' scene that shows candidate designs failing one by one, each with a one-line reason, would turn design choices into discovery.
Orchestrator: open with a stated question backlog and tick items off on screen; it doubles as roadmap and callback.
Evals: check that a lesson names the misconception it defuses and places the correction after the learner has a chance to object.
Ghost hands: for physical lessons, let a character 'drive the boat' (drag objects through the sim) before explaining wobble.
quote: wouldn't they absorb more energy and so heat up the water
